label: knob-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being short, thick and rounded at its free end, like a knob. NOTE: Not PATO:0002427 knobbled, which is a surface bearing many minute rounded projections; knob-like is the form of the whole structure (reduced anthers, tubercles, calluses).
reason: Used across three floras for the shape of a whole small structure. PATO's knobbled is a surface feature and capitate (FLOPO:0991006) means a stalked head, so neither fits.
A count of flowers (flowered → flower in flora_counted_parts.tsv) given as 'many'. It is held as a non-numeric count, the same way the review handled 'solitary or few'.
The negation of channeled, which the previous review (C196) mapped to PATO:0002255 grooved.
A count of flowers given as 'numerous', handled like 'many-flowered': the counted part is the flower and the value is not numeric.

In these floras it describes an outline broadest at the apex and tapering to the base (petals, leaflets, capsules), which is the wedge shape of PATO cuneate. A separate 'inverse' class would repeat that meaning.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: margin) + scabrous (FLOPO:0991058)
reason: Two things joined in one word: a part (the margin) and a value already in FLOPO (scabrous). Annotate the margin of the bearer as scabrous.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: margin) + straight (PATO_0002180)
reason: A region plus a value: the margins or sides of the leaflet or fruit apex are straight. No new term is needed.
A capsule drawn in at intervals between the seeds is constricted. Regular bead-like constriction is already moniliform (FLOPO:0991168), and 'when dry' goes to pattern 06 (specimen condition).
The prefix 'sub-' means 'nearly', applied to an existing FLOPO value, as with 'suborbicular' in pattern 01.
A vining or liana-like plant grows upward supported by other objects. The French 'vimineuse' means with long whip-like twigs (virgate, FLOPO:0991038), so check those statements separately.
States that glandular hairs are missing, which is the absence of PO:0004509 glandular trichome. 'With few' in the pedicel example is a count, not an absence.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer): vascular bundle (PO_0005020) + brown (FLOPO_0988003)
reason: A part plus a colour: the veins of the organ are brown. No new term is needed.
Breaking readily without bending matches PATO brittle.
'Hardly thickened' says the style base or pedicel is not noticeably thickened, so it is the negation of PATO increased thickness (synonym thickened).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer): plant cell (PO_0009002) + increased size (PATO_0000586)
reason: The cells of the part are large, so the cell is the bearer of the size. The 'celled → locule' entry in flora_counted_parts.tsv must not split this word.
The negation of geniculate, which the previous review (C191) mapped to PATO:0000617 bent.
The negation of the existing PATO orientation quality spreading.
A shallow or partial channel on the leaf acumen is 'nearly' the grooved value used for canaliculate (C194).
'1-spiked' and '3-8-spiked' count the spikes of an inflorescence. It needs a reviewed 'spiked → spike' row in flora_counted_parts.tsv.
Stalkless glands, scales and anthers are sessile in the botanical sense.
The colour is purple, and 'tinged' only says how strong it is, which is an RDF note. 'On ribs' or 'on front edge' go to the region-of-the-bearer pattern.
'Clearly defined' veinlets and alar regions are clearly visible, the reading the previous review gave 'distinct' (C176).

label: disintegrating
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's tissue breaking down with age into fibres or fragments while still attached to the plant. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991021 exfoliating (outer layers peel off in sheets) and FLOPO:0991026 fibrous; not PATO:0000639 degenerate, which is a pathological decline.
reason: A recurring character of leaf sheaths, ocreae, prophylls and bracts (palms, Polygonaceae) that no existing value covers.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values): ovate (PATO_0001891) – lanceolate (PATO_0001877)
reason: Two existing shape values joined in one word; ovoid is an exact synonym of PATO ovate.
A half-ring (a curved embryo, a disc or staminode around half the ovary) is crescent-shaped. It is not 'nearly ring-shaped'.
The name of the trait, not a value. The examples carry their own values (sessile, free, connate), which already have terms.
Cirriform means slender and curling like a tendril, which matches PATO tendrilous ('slender and spirally coiled').

target: cystolith (no PO class; needs a FLOPO anatomy class) present
reason: States that cystoliths are present in the leaf blade or stipule. Neither PO nor the FLOPO anatomy classes has a cystolith yet, so the rule needs that bearer class first.
A surface marked by glands sunk in small pits is covered by gland-dotted ('dots that are glands on or within its tissue').
A leaf or fruit ending in a long tip is acuminate.
